alignments.note: ὅστις → *who*.
λατρεύουσιν → *serve*; the ASV fronts it before its datives, which rule 15 permits.

The ASV recasts the dative with a supplied relative frame *that which is* plus a determiner; these are rule 7 helpers on the first dative noun, which is what the frame is predicated of, headed on the lexical noun *copy*.
καί → *and*.
σκιᾷ → *shadow*, sharing the frame already carried by ὑποδείγματι.

Rule 102: an article whose complement is a substantival adjective takes both the determiner and the supplied nominal, so *of the … things* is the article's, discontinuously under rule 15, headed on the supplied noun as rule 102 requires.
Substantival ἐπουρανίων left bare as *heavenly*, the article having taken the determiner and nominal under rule 102.
καθώς → *even as*; rule 82 records the comparative adverb taking *even as* and never *so*, headed on *as*.
Μωϋσῆς → *Moses*.

χρηματίζω → *is warned of God*; the italicized *of God* is the supplied completion of the lexeme's own sense and a rule 7 helper on the verb, rule 11 keeping the italics from making it `added`. Rule 91 heads on the word glossing the lexeme, *warned*.
Participle μέλλων with a supplied subordinator *when* and subject, both rule 7 helpers on a participle under rule 86, headed on *about*.
Infinitive with its own rule 7 marker, no preposition governing it (rule 61); ASV margin *complete*.
Rule 19: article → *the*.
σκηνήν → *tabernacle*.
γάρ → *for*, standing at the head of the quotation in the ASV.
Imperative Ὅρα → *See*.
φησίν → *saith he*, headed on the verb under rule 9.

Rule 86: the ASV subordinates a clause whose Greek is a bare future indicative with no conjunction governing it, so no source token licenses the complementizer. γάρ is already spent on *for* and no participle stands here, which is exactly rule 86's case.
ποιήσεις → *thou make*, headed on the lexical verb under rule 9.
Rule 17's generic-noun clause: a substantival adjective expanded with *things* heads on the adjective, *all things* on *All*.
κατά → *according to*, headed on the prepositional word.
Rule 19: article → *the*.
τύπον → *pattern*.
Second attributive article governing an expressed head noun τύπον: rule 31 leaves it `unrepresented` and gives the relativizer to the participle.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; relativizer and copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7, 9 and 31, headed on *showed*.
σοι → *thee*.
ἐν → *in*.
Rule 19: article → *the*.
ὄρει → *mount*.

review_notes: τῶν ἐπουρανίων follows rule 102: the article takes *of the … things* and the substantival adjective is left bare.
The supplied *that* before *thou make* is `added` under rule 86, no source token in the clause carrying the subordination.
*of God* folds onto κεχρημάτισται as the lexeme's own supplied completion rather than being marked `added`.
